newsitem.title: UK: UK's BAA November passengers up 9.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's BAA November passengers up 9.1 pct.

text.p: British airports operators BAA Plc said on Thursday that traffic at its seven UK airports rose 9.1 percent in November to 7.1 million passengers, compared to the same month last year.

The company said the rise was the largest monthly increase since March, with an underlying growth of 8.3 percent after adjusting for the effects of the closing of the Channel Tunnel operated by Anglo-French firm Eurotunnel.
It estimated the tunnel closure, caused by a blaze, boosted BAA's airport traffic by 50,000 passengers in November.
All of BAA's international markets recorded strong growth in November, with a 13.3 percent growth in North Atlantic traffic and a 10.9 percent rise in other long-haul traffic, it said.

European scheduled market, the only market to benefit from the tunnel closure, saw a growth of 7.7 percent compared with the same period last year, representing an underlying increase of 5.5 percent, BAA said in a statement.
European charter traffic -- which had dropped throughout the summer -- increased by 10.8 percent.
Among individual airports, traffic at Heathrow rose 6.1 percent year-on-year, while Gatwick increased by 18 percent and Stansted rose by 13.9 percent.
Glasgow recorded growth of 4.3 percent, its first monthly increase since April, BAA said.
